headline: The watch learns the knot — one shell downs two warheads
lede: Missile Command's autopilot now plays the arcade expert's deep-wave economy: it holds fire for crossings, spends one shell per ring where the geometry pays, and defends the silos first because a silo is ten more shells. The measured ceiling — volume is volume — is written down honestly with the two doctrines that failed.

notes.text: KNOT: under a measured magazine deficit the gunner holds a warhead, re-solving each tick, and fires one shell where the blast envelope provably catches two or more (predicted and actual, pinned in missilecmdcheck 133/0; wave-9 cities avg 3.00 -> 3.33, deepest-wave stalls 6 -> 5 across 12 seeds).
SILO-FIRST: when the raid outgrows the magazine, silo streams are answered before city streams — a dead silo forfeits the shells loaded in it exactly when you need them.

Measured and REJECTED, so nobody re-buys: 'sacrifice one city' (dead structures retarget the spawn dice — nothing absorbs leaks) and a ferry-chain reserve (the shells it saves are the shells the debt already counts). Deep waves stay volume losses by the port's own spawn law; PROVEN_WAVES stays 5.

A surviving mutant paid for itself: the strong-half readiness window never changed an outcome, so it was deleted — the 2 px envelope cushion is the real dud-guard. Doctrine got smaller, gains identical.
